Abstract: Solvent-induced electronic effects exist for intervalence charge-transfer reactions involving complexes of the type (2,2'-bipyridine)2ClRuII(pyrazine)Run,(NH3)4L4+,<sup>where L=</sup> NH3<sup>orvarious</sup> pyrazyl, pyridyl,<sup>or</sup> polypyridyl ligands. Specifically the following are found: (1) Mixing between appropriate donor and acceptor metal orbitals can be influenced substantially by<sup>thenature ofthesolvent.</sup> (2)<sup>The metal-metalinteraction</sup> energy, Rn,<sup>isalso affected.</sup> (3)<sup>Fromthesolvent</sup> effects,<sup>intervalence</sup> transfer appears to follow (in part) a hole-transfer pathway. 

Recently, Chang, Fung,<sup>andCurtisdescribedtheresultsofa</sup> study<sup>of</sup> optical<sup>intervalencetransfer</sup> (eq 1)<sup>asafunction of solvent</sup> in a series of (bpy)2ClRuII(pyz)Ru,II(NH3)4L4+ complexes (bpy = 2,2'-bipyridine; pyz = pyrazine; L = NH3 or various pyrazyl, pyridyl,<sup>or</sup> polypyridyl ligands).1 Their goal was to understand (bpy)2ClRun(pyz)Runi(NH3)4L4+ —* (bpy)2ClRuIII(pyz)RuII(NH3)4L4+* (1) the way in which specific solvent-ligand interactions can help to define the Franck-Condon barrier to charge transfer. We have recently<sup>discoveredthatthedetailed</sup> experimental<sup>information</sup> collected by them can also be used to understand another interesting<sup>issue:the</sup> way<sup>inwhichthesolventmodulates the electronic</sup> part<sup>oftheintervalence</sup> charge-transfer problem. We describe here three main findings: (1) Mixing between appropriate donor and acceptor metal orbitals involved in intramolecular charge transfer can be influenced substantially by the nature of the external solvent. (2) The metal-metal interaction energy, Hn, is also affected by solvent.2 (3)<sup>Fromthesolvent</sup> effects,<sup>in-</sup> tervalence transfer in reactions like eq 1 appears to follow (in part) a hole-transfer pathway.
